provenance.note: Krishnagiri district's rivers, groundwater and industry (scope krishnagiri-rivers; the district's own scope id is tn-krishnagiri). The district boundary is the frame and TN WRD's sub-basins, clipped to it, are the catchments (shedId): the Thenpennai's to the east, the Cauvery's Chinnar and Dodda Halla to the south-west. The industry register holds only units TNGIS matched to a land parcel, so every count is a lower bound; sector comes from the reviewed TNPCB type-code lookup pipeline-inputs/basins/krishnagiri-rivers/tnpcb-type-sectors.json.

properties.name: Thenpennai at Chokkarasanapalli (interstate entry point)
properties.purpose: TNPCB's monthly sampling of the river as it enters Tamil Nadu, ordered by the NGT joint committee (O.A. 111 of 2020); the Supreme Court's order of 7.7.2017 in O.S. No. 2 of 2015 set joint monthly sampling here from September 2017
properties.samplingBy: District Environmental Engineer, TNPCB, Hosur; analysed at the Advanced Environmental Laboratory, TNPCB, Salem (2017 to 2021 sheets) and the District Environmental Laboratory (2025 to 2026)
properties.samplesFiled: 53 dated samples, 2017-09-20 to 2026-01-28; none filed for May 2021 to March 2025 (2022-23 and 2023-24 reported as ranges)
properties.positionNote: CPCB NWMP station 'THENPENNAIYAR AT CHOKKARASANAHALLI BRIDGE (BANGALORE)' as printed on the National Water Data Portal (surface water quality, CPCB, Tamil Nadu resources); TNPCB's sheets print no coordinates

properties.name: Agara drain (NGT joint committee, 9 to 10 September 2020)
properties.sampledBy: NGT joint committee (CPCB, KSPCB, TNPCB and the departments named in the order of 20.07.2020), following CPCB's NWMP standard operating procedure (August 2017)
properties.designatedBestUseClass: E: Irrigation, industrial cooling, controlled waste disposal
properties.reportFindings: Dissolved oxygen above 4 mg/L only at the Kelavarapalli reservoir, its outfall, the Y junction and the Bellandur diversion channel; the river is oxygen-depleted from Channasandra bridge to Bagalur bridge (section 5.2). BOD fails the designated-best-use criteria at every sampled location; at Bagalur bridge (53 mg/L) it exceeds even the general effluent discharge standard (section 5.2). Anionic surfactants were found only at Sokkarasanapalli and Bagalur bridge (section 5.2; Table 2 prints 0.34 and 0.43 mg/L). Iron above the permissible level at Mugalur bridge, Sokkarasanapalli, Bagalur and Kodiyalam; zinc at Channasandra bridge and Kelavarapalli; mercury in Bellandur lake (0.012 mg/L) (section 5.2, Table 3). No pesticide traces at any location (section 5.2). Rainfall of more than 100 mm fell on the night before sampling, 9 September 2020 (section 5.2).
properties.positionNote: Agara Lake (OSM relation 8469370), centre; the printed table's coordinate column is blank, so the point is placed by name

properties.name: Channasandra bridge (CPCB, KSPCB and TNPCB joint sampling, 28 October 2024)
properties.sampledBy: CPCB Regional Directorate Bengaluru with KSPCB (Regional Office Sarjapura) and TNPCB (Regional Office Hosur); stretch of 34.8 km from Channasandra bridge to the Kelavarapalli dam
properties.reportFindings: Water quality at all six locations fails the primary water quality criteria for bathing waters (Environment (Protection) Amendment Rules, 2000) (reply, paragraph 7). Dissolved oxygen below detection up to Chokkarasanapalli; froth seen at Chokkarasanapalli, the dam outfall and the Mitteganahalli bridge (Table 2). TNPCB's own monthly sampling at Chokkarasanapalli for 2022-23 and 2023-24: BOD 32 to 134 mg/L, total coliform 1,200 to 20,050 and fecal coliform 840 to 16,520 MPN/100ml (reply, paragraph 8(e)).
properties.positionNote: Coordinates as the report's Table 2 prints them
